note: Anti-PD-1 monotherapy in unselected advanced HCC: accelerated approvals on phase 1/2 response rates, then both confirmatory monotherapy phase 3s (CheckMate-459, KEYNOTE-240) missed overall survival; the clinical antibodies do not bind mouse PD-1, so every mouse HCC result comes from a rat anti-mouse surrogate.
label: HCC (anti-PD-1)

engagement.model: Syngeneic orthotopic mouse HCC (HCA-1, RIL-175; later Hepa1-6 and hydrodynamic-injection models) dosed with a rat anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate
engagement.note: Nivolumab/pembrolizumab do not bind mouse PD-1; mouse HCC work used a rat anti-mouse surrogate, and no HCC-patient PD-1 occupancy comparison was published.
engagement.short: Surrogate antibody; no patient occupancy comparison
engagement.quote: In separate experiments, antibody blockade of the programmed death ligand-1 receptor programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) showed antitumor effects in treatment-naive tumors in orthotopic (grafted and genetically engineered) models of HCC.
engagement.reason: Product never dosed in mouse HCC
engagement.judgement: Called untested rather than same: the only published mouse-to-patient juxtaposition (Pfister 2021) compares intratumoral PD1+ cell counts between anti-PD1-treated NASH and viral HCC patients, which is cross-sectional and not a drug-engagement readout. Class-level receptor occupancy (nivolumab phase 1, non-HCC tumours) was measured in patients, not predicted by a model. Abstract-level reading of Chen 2015; the FDA nivolumab pharmacology review (2014) states verbatim 'Nivolumab does not recognize mouse PD-1' and names the chimeric rat clone 4H2 as the surrogate, dosed in J558/MC38/SA1/N (no liver model).

dose.model: Syngeneic orthotopic mouse HCC (HCA-1, RIL-175) dosed with a rat anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate
dose.note: Surrogate dosed ~10 mg/kg in mice; clinical HCC dose came from non-HCC phase 1 occupancy; CheckMate 040 saw no dose-response over 0.1-10 mg/kg.
dose.short: Mouse dose never mapped to patients
dose.quote: In separate experiments, antibody blockade of the programmed death ligand-1 receptor programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) showed antitumor effects in treatment-naive tumors in orthotopic (grafted and genetically engineered) models of HCC.
dose.judgement: No HCC model produced an exposure or occupancy target for patients: the HCC doses (nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w -> 240 mg; pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w) were carried over from receptor-occupancy plateaus in non-HCC phase 1 patients. CheckMate 040 (El-Khoueiry 2017, doi 10.1016/S0140-6736(17)31046-2) escalated 0.1-10 mg/kg in HCC patients: 'Incidence of treatment-related adverse events did not seem to be associated with dose and no maximum tolerated dose was reached.' The FDA review's 4H2 dose-ranging in SA1/N mice (0.3-30 mg/kg) is also nearly flat, but no source puts the two side by side, so this stays untested rather than same.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic orthotopic mouse HCC (HCA-1, RIL-175; grafted and genetically engineered) dosed with a rat anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate
efficacy.note: Anti-mouse PD-1 alone had antitumour effects in treatment-naive orthotopic HCC; added to sorafenib only with CXCR4 blockade. No patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: Surrogate anti-PD-1 slows orthotopic mouse HCC
efficacy.quote: In separate experiments, antibody blockade of the programmed death ligand-1 receptor programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) showed antitumor effects in treatment-naive tumors in orthotopic (grafted and genetically engineered) models of HCC.
efficacy.judgement: Earliest in vivo anti-PD-1 antibody study in a mouse HCC model that PubMed returned (two searches, 2005-2016); Sawada 2014/2015 (Int J Oncol, GPC3 vaccine + anti-PD-1 in tumour-bearing mice) is contemporaneous. Abstract-level reading. The pivotal nivolumab FDA pharmacology package used no liver model at all, so no company-filed HCC model exists; the academic orthotopic models are what the field relied on.

efficacy.model: Choline-deficient high-fat-diet NASH-HCC mice vs non-NASH mouse liver-cancer models, dosed with rat anti-mouse PD-1 (RMP1-14)
efficacy.note: NASH-HCC mice did not regress on anti-PD1 while non-NASH models did; pooled CheckMate-459/KEYNOTE-240/IMbrave150 showed no survival gain in non-viral HCC (HR 0.92).
efficacy.short: Etiology split in mice matched patients
efficacy.quote: A meta-analysis of three randomized phase III clinical trials that tested inhibitors of PDL1 (programmed death-ligand 1) or PD1 in more than 1,600 patients with advanced HCC revealed that immune therapy did not improve survival in patients with non-viral HCC.
efficacy.reason: Mouse etiology split reproduced in trials
efficacy.judgement: Same, not contra, is the call. The source itself puts mouse and patient results side by side (full text read via PMC8046670): 'None of the pre-existing liver tumours regressed in response to anti-PD1 therapy' in NASH mice, whereas 'other (non-NASH) mouse models of liver cancer ... reacted to PD1 immunotherapy with tumour regression'; in the pooled trials viral-HCC patients benefited (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.48-0.94) and non-viral did not (HR 0.92, 0.77-1.11; interaction P = 0.03). Direction-only agreement on a subgroup; the pool includes atezolizumab+bevacizumab (PD-L1, IMbrave150) alongside the two anti-PD-1 monotherapy phase 3s. Not contra because the unselected-population misses (KEYNOTE-240 OS HR 0.781, P = 0.0238 vs one-sided 0.0174, Finn 2020 doi 10.1200/JCO.19.01307; CheckMate-459 OS HR 0.85, P = 0.075 vs 0.0419, Yau 2022 doi 10.1016/S1470-2045(21)00604-5) were near-misses in the model's direction, and no published source states that a mouse HCC model predicted wrongly. Caveat: the mouse experiments were run after the trials read out, so the comparison is retrospective, and the paper notes species gaps (no cirrhosis in mice). Population kept Unselected because etiology is not a prescribing criterion. model_first_use_year on this entry is 2021 because the NASH model's first use for the class is the comparison itself; the conventional syngeneic model opens the strip at 2015.

registry_detail.trial: CheckMate 040 (phase 1/2, basis of the accelerated approval)
KEYNOTE-224 (phase 2, basis of the accelerated approval)

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4- and 13-week repeat-dose toxicology (nivolumab, up to 50 mg/kg); no HCC-specific safety model
safety.note: Monkeys showed no autoimmune disease at 42x clinical exposure; patients' commonest AEs were immune-mediated, incl. hepatotoxicity; CheckMate 040 escalation saw 25% grade 3/4 related AEs.
safety.quote: Monkeys did not develop any clear signs of the autoimmune toxicity seen in clinical trials with nivolumab, however, the generalized lymphocytic infiltration and increases in memory T cells do hint at the possibility of these types of toxicities.
safety.judgement: The FDA review itself makes the comparison ('In patients receiving nivolumab, autoimmune disturbances are the most commonly reported adverse events including, among others, immune-mediated pneumonitis, colitis, hepatotoxicity, thyroid toxicity, and nephritis' versus 'no evidence of autoimmune disease was observed in the monkey toxicology studies'), so comparison_stated is true, but the patients compared were the pre-2014 melanoma/NSCLC/RCC trial population, not HCC. The HCC context inherits this model because the HCC supplements rested on the original nonclinical package; HCC-specific patient data (CheckMate 040, El-Khoueiry 2017, doi 10.1016/S0140-6736(17)31046-2): 12/48 (25%) grade 3/4 treatment-related AEs in escalation, serious related AEs included 'liver disorder', and the authors called the profile manageable with 'no new signals'. Medium confidence because the review hedges that infiltrates 'hint' at the toxicity, and because PD-1 knockout mouse autoimmunity (cited in the review as mechanistic rationale, not as a submitted tox model) did point the right way. Not verified from an HCC-specific sBLA review that no new nonclinical safety study was filed for HCC.
